inspections.finding: The complete initial vav ends in a wide, flat basal platform joined to its long shaft. The attached bar does not uniquely distinguish a literal patah from compressed paired dots, a shortened stem or a heavy ordinary terminal. Literal bar/pair/stem/single-node and full-vav sheva/ordinary foot controls do not defeat those competitors. Retain the vowel disclosure without claiming source absence; refresh only its anchor for the separately certified yod point.

The complete yod head recedes on its lower left, then re-expands into a distinct low-left lobe beside a continuing right tail. This branch reproduces the paired15 pointed-yod contour and the same-unit vayokhal pointed yod; the detached36 dot fixes the branch position. The paired15 plain yod, same-unit heshiv plain yod and heavier yehi/ki plain controls retain an exposed tail or small ordinary terminal instead of this low-left branch after recession. The result rests on the full contour, not width, a white hole or expected spelling. Append BC after existing B8 and preserve every previous scalar.

The complete initial vav has one broad opaque foot below a continuous shaft. Neither a detached point nor a uniquely shaped added contour can be isolated. Literal bar, horizontal pair, stem and single-node classes, plus full-vav sheva and ordinary vav foot, leave competing explanations for the merged base. Retain the vowel note without claiming source absence.

The Daniel yod has a broad opaque lower-left mass and a continuing right tip, but only a shallow recession beneath its head. Heavy plain yehi/ki impressions demonstrate left-hooking terminals, while the pointed paired15 and same-unit vayokhal controls have a distinct branch after recession. Here an equally heavy ordinary impression still competes with a merged dagesh; width alone cannot certify the point. Retain the exact Daniel note and its sole physical occurrence.
